name: MOJI (Meet Up, Now!)
subtitle: A web service for matching and managing small-group meetups
intention: A platform that breaks down communication barriers between departments and cohorts on campus, so anyone can easily create and run a meetup around a shared interest or goal (projects, study groups).
behindStory: As vice president of a club, I tried to set up collaborations and joint study groups with other clubs, but ran into the problem that there was no channel on campus to connect us. To bring scattered student meetups together and broaden students' collaboration experience, I led the planning and development myself.

features.title: API gateway for unified MSA logging
features.summary: Built a single entry point with Spring Cloud Gateway and consolidated JWT authentication to remove duplication
features.detail: Standardized request/response logs from distributed microservices so they are collected in one place, and centralized the auth filter at the gateway to share authorization logic across services.

features.title: Refactoring the monolith into microservices (MSA)
features.summary: Split into Auth, MAIN and Chat services and set up independent deployment
features.detail: Chose a separate database for each service (MySQL/MongoDB) to improve availability, and built REST-based communication between services to strengthen stability.

troubleShooting.problem: The entire service went down under server load while developing the chat feature
troubleShooting.cause: The chat service was merged onto a single AWS free-tier instance, exceeding its resource limits
troubleShooting.solution: Expanded infrastructure with server resources provided by the university and fully separated the chat service, introducing a microservice (MSA) structure
troubleShooting.result: Failure isolation keeps other features working even if chat fails, and standardized errors make real-time monitoring easier

planning.title: Meetup registration
planning.description: Register the meetup information and set the headcount, period and description

planning.title: Meetup matching
planning.description: Apply to join; the organizer accepts or declines to confirm members

planning.title: Chat
planning.description: A real-time chat room for confirmed meetup members

planning.title: Categories
planning.description: Find meetups by type (projects, study groups) and tags

retrospective.label: What went well
retrospective.text: After a single-server outage, I separated the chat service and split the system into Auth, MAIN and Chat, building a failure-isolated, independently deployable structure on my own.

retrospective.label: What I'd improve
retrospective.text: I didn't track the project's progress with concrete metrics. If I had recorded traffic and bottlenecks as metrics before the transition, it would have been a better-grounded decision.

retrospective.label: What I learned
retrospective.text: Solid architectural design matters more than technology itself. I experienced firsthand that, depending on the service architecture, the same service can cut costs significantly and secure availability.

name: Beeper
subtitle: A real-time video-call volunteer matching service for people less comfortable with digital technology
intention: A real-time assistance platform that removes everyday barriers such as kiosks and online reservations for older adults and others less comfortable with digital tools with just their voice, and matches them by video call with volunteers on standby.
behindStory: I noticed a contradiction: for seniors, even the "sign up and write a post" steps of existing apps are a huge barrier. I concluded that seeing and speaking are more intuitive and faster than chat, and planned a zero-barrier service: "speak and it becomes a request; accept it and you are face to face right away."

features.title: One-touch help requests by voice recognition
features.summary: STT (Speech-to-Text) integration and FCM push notifications for users who are not logged in
features.detail: Requests are created automatically from microphone input, users can correct misrecognized text, and notifications are sent and received via FCM tokens with no sign-up to remove barriers.

features.title: Concurrency control and a signaling server
features.summary: Guaranteed first-come matching with conditional DB updates and connected WebRTC P2P calls through a WebSocket relay
features.detail: Ensured that only one volunteer succeeds when many accept at once, and routed WebRTC session information (SDP/ICE) accurately to the matched peer with a WebSocket handler.

features.title: DB design for matching standby and history management
features.summary: ERD optimized for filtering by waiting status and automatically storing history when a call ends
features.detail: Mapped volunteer availability status to notification preference tags and designed a normalized model so that data accumulates into activity statistics without loss when a call ends.

troubleShooting.problem: Multiple volunteers accepted the same request at once, causing duplicate matches
troubleShooting.cause: Reading the state (Select) and updating it (Update) were separate steps in the accept API, creating a race condition
troubleShooting.solution: Used a single-query update with a WHERE status = 'WAITING' condition for atomic first-come handling
troubleShooting.result: Fully eliminated duplicate matches at the DB level without the cost of a distributed lock

troubleShooting.problem: Signals were lost because the WebRTC offer/answer exchange timing did not line up
troubleShooting.cause: The senior and the volunteer joined the socket room at different times, so early signaling messages were lost
troubleShooting.solution: Had the signaling server track room-join order and send the offer only after confirming both sides had joined
troubleShooting.result: Brought the video-call connection failure rate on first accept close to zero and secured call stability

planning.title: Voice help request
planning.description: Create a request just by speaking, with no sign-up or typing

planning.title: Volunteer matching
planning.description: Notify waiting volunteers and connect with the first one to accept

planning.title: Real-time video call
planning.description: Help while seeing each other and sharing the screen, instead of chatting

planning.title: Activity history
planning.description: Volunteer activity is recorded and accumulated automatically after each call

retrospective.label: What went well
retrospective.text: Within just one month, I traced the root causes of the two core problems — concurrency (first-come matching) and signaling timing — and solved them.

retrospective.label: What I'd improve
retrospective.text: With so little time, I could not do enough automated testing or load testing. I wish I had left a concurrent-request test for the accept API in the codebase.

retrospective.label: What I learned
retrospective.text: Planning to lower users' barriers ended up shaping technical choices too (FCM without login, voice input), and atomicity can be secured with query conditions instead of a distributed lock.
